visuals.label: Figure 1
visuals.caption: Overview of JevVLA. A lightweight Jev-inspired scalar energy adapts frozen robot policies: its values compare action candidates, while its action gradients provide bounded corrections or guide generation. Benchmarks share the core architecture and use independently trained weights. Robot scenes are local simulator renders used as illustrations, not JevVLA rollout frames. Bars show the test-set gains in Table 1. CLIPort reports strict terminal success from closed-loop execution. Direct evaluates the same frozen base policy without JevVLA.

visuals.label: Figure 2
visuals.caption: JevVLA architecture. Fixed encodings connect observations and native action proposals from a frozen policy to a conditional energy core. The core combines a quadratic potential with a nonlinear scalar residual. Its values rank candidates, optionally with the policy prior, while its action gradients provide bounded corrections or guide iterative generation. Execution feedback, expert corrections, or demonstration preferences supervise energy values and action gradients as available; training updates only the adapter. Benchmarks share the 79,817-parameter core architecture and learn separate weights. Robot images illustrate the computation.

visuals.label: Figure 8
visuals.caption: Candidate selection on CLIPort. The upper case (seed 3900000155) changes the first proposal from c0 to c1; frozen-policy continuation then places both orange blocks in pink bowls. The lower case (seed 3900000148) selects c3, which moves a yellow bowl into the white bowl while leaving the orange block outside. Candidate overlays show recorded pick and place positions on the same initial heightmap. Displayed scores are ∆U = U(ci) −U(c0), with E = −U. Camera frames replay the four recorded branches with the frozen base policy. The aggregate CLIPort evaluation covers 1,800 test examples.
